profile.headline: Software Developer at Central City Concern
profile.summary: I am a software developer on a multi-disciplinary Agile/Scrum team at Central City Concern. I primarily work with athenaHealth Practice Solution, developing suites of forms for implementation using the Medical Enrichment Language (MEL).

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description:
Day to Day:
* Validate, review, configure, and adapt enterprise software solutions across the agency using Agile and Scrum
* Create, Update, and Refactor forms for athenaHealth Practice Solution (APS) using our solution development lifecycle to determine what the end user wants and needs. Forms are written in MEL in our development environment, tested in our training environment, then finally deployed into production for the end user.   
* Answer service requests from end users regarding issues with any of our software solutions, both enterprise and those built in house. 

As a Member of a Team:
* Upgraded APS across Health Services, changing tools and workflows for hundreds of employees and altering hundreds of workstations.
* Implemented APS at three (and counting) different locations in the agency, one recuperative care facility, one substance use facility, and one detoxification center
* Learned, customized, and implemented Visualutions' GroupFocus (an add on to athenaHealth that allows counselors to bulk create clinical documentation for an entire substance use or mental health group) at a facility 
* Implemented Fusion's eMAR, an electronic medication distribution record, received feedback from end users, and worked with the company to develop a product that better suited our needs
* Actively participated in the growth, development, and maturation of our solution development life cycle and our use of Agile, Scrum, and Design Thinking. Over two years, we have taken the tools on hand and made them work for our teams and have seen buy in from other teams in the agency. 

Maybe Most Importantly:
* Developed empathy and some perspective working with people who have dedicated their lives to helping hundreds of other people succeed on a daily basis

positions.title: Grade 7 Homeroom Teacher, Curriculum Coordinator
positions.description:
* Effective communicator and collaborator.

* Had to think quickly to solve problems as they arose, frequently handling multiple tasks at once (e.g. being Curriculum Coordinator, Prefect of Discipline, substitute teacher, and public face of the school to the parents). 

* Learned to effectively communicate with people from all backgrounds

* Lead weekly faculty meetings to discuss upcoming events and any issues that arose during the week.

* Worked on different sides of an organization, as both employee and administrator, gaining a unique understanding of how to reconcile the needs of an employee and the needs of an administration.

* Was responsible for constructing and maintaining curriculum.

* Was responsible for professional development, event planning, and interactions with parents.

* Constructed a detailed and thorough discipline system that was able to be flexible depending on the needs and ages of the students.

positions.title: Teacher
positions.description:
Between 2002 and 2014, I was a teacher. I taught Middle School Language Arts, English as a Foreign Language to children, adolescents, and adults, and most recently took an administrative role as the Curriculum Coordinator for a small international school.

I started working in Portland, OR, then worked in Shenzhen and Zhuhai, China,  Boston, MA, Honolulu, HI, Tainan and Kaohsiung, Taiwan.

projects.title: FitMap
projects.description:
FitMap is a fitness app that we created during our internship at Development Now. Over the course of five weeks, we developed an app from start to finish, utilizing the resources of Development Now and learning more about a focused development process, from creation to execution. 

FitMap tracks your steps as you walk and converts those steps into the calories you burned. It uses Google Maps to give you multiple routes to your destination and tells you how many calories walking each route would burn. You can also use FitMap to track the food you've eaten throughout the day to keep track of the calories you've consumed. 

All this data is saved on the internal SQLite database for future reference. This is a work in progress and more features will be updated as we continue to work on it. 

Technologies Used:
* Android Studio
* SQLite
* Google Maps API
* Nutritionix API

View our repo on GitHub:
https://github.com/vrdlc/FitMap

projects.title: Fridg
projects.description:
Fridg is an app that helps users create a persistent grocery list. Once an item is purchased, swipe, and the item moves to a pantry list, a living record of what you have in your kitchen. When you run out of something, swipe again and it moves back to your grocery list. 

I designed this app to be as simple as possible, as most to-do list and note taking apps aren't, frequently taking multiple clicks to access a list every single time the app was accessed. Fridge automatically opens to your list and keeps focus on it even when it's not being actively viewed. 

View my repo on GitHub at: https://github.com/vrdlc/FridgAndroid or connect to it on the About page of the app.

Technologies Used:
*Android Studio
*Firebase(Legacy)

Future updates will include:
* Updated Firebase functionality
* Users will have the ability to share lists with each other, so a family can, for instance, alter the same list
* Add photos to item listings
* Add user generated categories that will be used to sort items (dairy, produce, meat, cleaning, etc)
